messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: [redacted] 
Age: 28 years 
Sex: Female 

Date of Admission: [redacted] 
Date of Discharge: [redacted]

Reason for Admission:
The patient presented with right hip pain after a fall and was diagnosed with a pathologic hip fracture. 

Clinical Course:
Following admission, the patient underwent radiographic and imaging studies which revealed lytic lesions in the femoral neck and intertrochanteric region as well as osseous destructive lesions in the lumbar spine. The bone scan was suggestive of metastatic disease. A biopsy revealed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with aggressive features and a germinal center subtype histology. The patient underwent a total right hip replacement and returned for follow-up evaluation.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was managed for the pathologic hip fracture and underwent biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis of lymphoma. Following diagnosis, the patient underwent a total right hip replacement. The patient is scheduled for further evaluation and management by the oncology team. 

Discharge Medications: 
See the oncology team. 

Follow-up Plan: 
The patient is to follow up with the oncology team. 

Discharge Condition: 
The patient is stable.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
**C83**

The principal diagnosis here is debatable, so this is a judgement call.

- **Choice:** The biopsy-confirmed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (C83.3) is the underlying condition that caused the fracture. It was newly diagnosed during this admission. On that basis I have taken it as the principal diagnosis.
- **Alternative:** The admission and the main procedure, a total hip replacement, were directed at the pathological fracture. Australian Coding Standard 0236 may support putting the fracture first when treatment targets that complication. If so, the principal code would be M84 (pathological fracture in neoplastic disease), with the lymphoma as an additional diagnosis.
- **Uncertainty:** I have not been able to confirm the exact wording of that standard or the fracture subcode. Please check ACS 0236 before finalising.
